items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — opened straight into 'how can I help you?' and moved to logistics.

No real agenda statement. Said 'I just need some contact information... we'll talk through inventory and access' but never gave the ~10-15 minute timeframe, so the customer had no idea this was a 23-minute call.

Never asked whether she needed packing services. She volunteered that she'd already packed boxes and later that the realtor wants personal items boxed up — a 3,000 sqft home going out in four phases is a packing-service conversation he never opened.

Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?') on a call where the customer twice volunteered stress (house not sold, realtor staging demands, 'might have to use you like four times').
No parking or truck-access probe at either the origin house or the storage facility — only asked about first vs. upper floor.

On-Time Guarantee named but gutted: said 'we're not going to be hours and hours late... not show up' and never delivered the actual differentiator, that we start discounting immediately if we miss the window.

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing. The 'stack boxes at dolly height' tip was the only prep guidance; no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill' framing, no consolidation examples (kids' toys, garden tools, loose items in drawers, photos off walls), no 'take a carload' tip.

No booking ask. Customer said she was choosing between Friday the 4th and Sunday the 6th and he warned availability tightens — then said only 'you would want to kind of get the spot held eventually.' Never asked for the date.
'No deposit required' never said. Got close with 'payments just taken at the end of the move with iPad card reader' but skipped the actual differentiator.

No confirmation-email handoff. Best he offered was 'I guess I could send the information over to' — hedged, and never promised a confirmation email, the bolded detail list, or 'reply with any corrections.'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave business hours or how to reach the branch.
Used the customer's name once in 23 minutes ('Alright, Jennifer') — and that was in the sign-off.
No time equivalents (school bus reference) and no traffic variable on an Austin-to-Houston drive he was quoting an 8-hour day for.
top_strength: The pricing and inclusions block was genuinely excellent — day-of-week tiers priced out concretely ($111/mover Friday vs. $105 Sunday, '$72 cheaper'), everything-included list (fuel, truck, taxes, insurance, blankets, shrink wrap, dollies, tool bag), and a real no-hidden-fees pitch naming credit card processing, stair fees, step fees, and change-of-inventory fees. His insurance explanation was the best part of the call: $2,000 No Worries handled in-house by the claims team, the 60 cents/lb state minimum for customer-packed boxes, and an honest negligence carve-out ('someone just flat out dropped the box... that's where we actually do step in'). He also solved problems he wasn't asked to solve — referred sparefoot.com unprompted for climate-controlled storage, explained the refundable $14/pad rental so items stay wrapped in storage, and surfaced the overnight hotel fee before it could become a surprise.
coaching_note: Daniel, the highest-leverage fix is Save Your Ass, and this call is the clearest possible example of why. Your customer is making four separate trips with 100 boxes and is actively trying to control cost — she is the single most receptive audience for the prep speech you'll get this month, and you gave her 'stack them at dolly height' and nothing else. You needed: 'Jennifer, the biggest lever on your bill is prep, because you're paying for time. Everything you consolidate before we get there is time you don't pay for — get the loose stuff out of drawers, pull the pictures off the walls yourself, box the garage odds and ends. And anything small enough to fit in your car, take a carload each time you drive over. On four trips that adds up fast. Does that make sense?' That's two minutes that would have cut her bill and your on-site hours. Second priority: you did all the hard work and then didn't ask for the sale. She told you she was picking between the 4th and the 6th, you told her availability tightens, and you closed with 'eventually.' Say it straight: 'Sunday saves you $72 and I've got it open right now — no deposit, nothing charged until the move is done. Want me to lock it in?' Third, small but cheap to fix: use her name three or four times, and finish every call with 'I'll send you a confirmation email with all this in it — reply with any corrections' plus 'any other questions before I let you go?'
phone_presence_notes: Real warmth and accommodation in spots ('take a second, that's totally fine,' handling the AC techs and restroom break gracefully, 'sometimes it clarifies it for you as well'), but long run-on monologues reduced the customer to bare 'Okay' more than twenty times and he used her name only once.
